title: Jolt Physics crashes on 32-bit Windows: MOVAPS into 8-byte-aligned allocations
body:
### Tested versions

- Reproducible in: 4.7.2.stable.mono (official Windows `x86_32` export template)
- Not reproducible in: the same project exported `x86_64` (any build)

### System information

Windows 11 Pro 10.0.26200 (WOW64, `Wow64Guest=0x014C`) - NVIDIA GeForce GTX 780 - Vulkan 1.2.142 Forward Mobile

### Issue description

An exported 32-bit Windows game using `physics/3d/physics_engine = "Jolt Physics"` crashes with `STATUS_ACCESS_VIOLATION (0xc0000005)` shortly after the first 3D scene with concave collision loads. The identical project exported for `x86_64` never crashes.

The faulting module is always the engine binary itself, never the game's own library. Across 10 crashes WER recorded three distinct fault offsets, and **every one of them is the same instruction encoding, `0F 29` = `MOVAPS m128, xmm`** — the 16-byte-*aligned* SSE store:

| Fault RVA           | Bytes at that offset                | Instruction                   |
| ------------------- | ----------------------------------- | ----------------------------- |
| `0x00CDDB80` (7/10) | `0F 29 0A 83 EA 80 0F 29 42 90 ...` | `movaps [edx], xmm1`          |
| `0x00B8FFA6` (2/10) | `0F 29 02 83 C7 0C 83 C3 01 ...`    | `movaps [edx], xmm0`          |
| `0x00BEF2A2` (1/10) | `0F 29 4C 02 10 8B B5 44 FF ...`    | `movaps [edx+eax+0x10], xmm1` |

Two full crash dumps give the register state at the fault:

```
dump 1:  EIP 0x00DFDB80   EDX 0x56FF2588   EDX % 16 = 8   ESI 0x0000C000 (48 KB buffer)
dump 2:  EIP 0x00DFDB80   EDX 0x57A5B248   EDX % 16 = 8   ESI 0x0000C000
```

`EDX` is the destination operand. **It is 8-byte aligned and never 16-byte aligned**, at two different absolute addresses. The 32-bit Windows CRT only guarantees 8-byte alignment from `malloc`; the x64 CRT guarantees 16, which is exactly why the same code path never faults on `x86_64`. Because each allocation is a coin flip, a scene that builds many shapes loses the flip almost immediately.

Note for anyone reproducing: `MOVAPS` on a misaligned operand raises **#GP, not #PF**, so there is no faulting address. Windows synthesises the exception record as `ExceptionInformation = {0, 0xFFFFFFFF}`, and reading `ExceptionInformation[1]` as an address yields a meaningless `0xFFFFFFFF`. The `{0, 0xFFFFFFFF}` pair *is* the misalignment signature; the real operand has to come from the thread `CONTEXT`.

### Where it points

The nearest identifying strings in the code region around `0x00B8FFA6` are from `modules/jolt_physics/shapes/jolt_concave_polygon_shape_3d.cpp` (`set_data`, `Condition "maybe_faces.get_type() != Variant::PACKED_VECTOR3_ARRAY" is true.`, `Condition "vertex_count < 3" is true. Returning: nullptr`), and the surrounding code reads a 12-byte stride and packs each element into a 16-byte slot — a `PackedVector3Array` being converted into Jolt's SIMD vector type.

The other two sites match Jolt structures as well: `0x00BEF2A2` writes 32-byte-strided records built by `minps`/`maxps`, which is `JPH::AABox` (`Vec3 mMin; Vec3 mMax`), and `0x00CDDB80` fills a 48 KB array of 128-byte entries with `+FLT_MAX` / `-FLT_MAX` splats, i.e. bounds initialisation.

`JPH::Vec3` is `__m128` and requires 16-byte alignment, so whatever allocator the module hands Jolt has to satisfy that. On 32-bit Windows the CRT allocator does not.

**Confirmed: setting `physics/3d/physics_engine = "GodotPhysics3D"` for the 32-bit build stops the crash entirely.** Same project, same machine, same scene — the only change was the physics engine.


### Steps to reproduce

The attached MRP builds 400 ConcavePolygonShape3D from a PackedVector3Array (512 triangles each). Export it for Windows and run it:

  x86_32 + Jolt Physics       → crashes on the FIRST shape
  x86_32 + GodotPhysics3D     → prints "FINISHED - no crash"
  x86_64 + Jolt Physics       → prints "FINISHED - no crash"

  Only the physics engine and the architecture change between those three runs.

  It reproduces under Wine on Linux, so no Windows machine is needed:

```
  $ wine JoltMRP.exe --headless
  Godot Engine v4.7.2.stable.official.ed1daf0bf - https://godotengine.org
  physics engine: Jolt Physics
  triangles per shape: 512
  wine: Unhandled illegal instruction at address 010E719B (thread 0168), starting debugger...
```

  Wine loads at the preferred image base, so 0x010E719B maps straight into .text:

```
  10e7193:  movdqa 0x59d9f10, %xmm0
  10e719b:  movaps %xmm0, (%eax)      ← faults here
  10e719e:  movdqa 0x59d9f20, %xmm0
  10e71a6:  movaps %xmm0, 0x10(%eax)
```

  Same MOVAPS m128, xmm as the three sites found in the original crash dumps. (Wine surfaces the #GP as illegal instruction where Windows surfaces it as
  0xc0000005; both are the same trap.)

### Minimal reproduction project (MRP)

[jolt-32bit-movaps-mrp.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/32074635/jolt-32bit-movaps-mrp.zip) — GDScript only, no C#, no imported assets. To use the prebuilt binary instead, override.cfg next to the exe with `[physics]` / `3d/physics_engine="GodotPhysics3D"` switches engines without re-exporting.
